_readme: SS-601. Every numeric performance claim on an indexable page must appear here.
Seeded 2026-08-20 from the pages themselves by scripts/build-page-index.mjs output --
no basis was invented. Each entry needs measurementBasis and dateMeasured filled in,
OR the claim removed from the page, OR the entry marked disposition:"not-a-claim"
where the match is prose rather than an assertion (the /case-studies "82% faster" is
the site ARGUING AGAINST opening with a figure, not making one).
BOTH fields are enforced as of 2026-08-27. Until then SS-601 read only measurementBasis,
so a row answered with a provenance and no date stopped warning and read as settled -- the
sentence above had promised otherwise since this file was written, which is the same gap as
the unimplemented not-a-claim disposition. A MISSING key counts exactly as TODO, so deleting
dateMeasured does not silence the check. A filled dateMeasured that is not an ISO date (or
two separated by / for a measurement spanning days) is an ERROR rather than a warning: it
looks answered and records nothing. A date after today is an error for the same reason.
PARTIAL ANSWERS KEEP THE TODO PREFIX, with what was answered written after it. A basis is
either sufficient to check the claim or it is not, and SS-601 reads any non-TODO value as
sufficient -- so half an answer left unprefixed silences the row. Write the half down; keep
the prefix. dateMeasured is different: a date is whole or absent, so it is filled outright.
occurrences is load-bearing: SS-601 errors when a page carries MORE instances of a
token than are registered, so adding a second unmeasured "27%" to a page that already
has a registered one is caught. It is not matched on context, because a typo fix
beside a claim should not turn the build red.
contextOnPage is verbatim page text, for triage only. It is not evidence of anything.
